correctness.rationale: The graph is defined unambiguously by the six quadratic-residue steps modulo 13. An exhaustive independent-subset partition implementation establishes chi=5, 377 unordered optimal color partitions and exactly 45,240 labeled colorings. It constructs every legal recoloring, obtains two components of 22,620 each, and checks 98,280 edges and global color-transposition swapping. A logically distinct vertex-by-vertex C++ enumeration reconstructs all 45,240 five-color and 4,502,160 six-color assignments, tests all recoloring edges by arithmetic state encoding, and finds respectively two and one components with matching five-color counts and 27,626,040 six-color edges. A third complete Grundy checker fixes a color-seven vertex using the graph translation action, permutes its six neighbors and checks all proper completions and lower-neighbor-color conditions, finding zero seven-Grundy colorings; degree six bounds Grundy at most seven. Hence the Grundy number is at most six and the cited Bonamy-Bousquet theorem gives connectivity for all k>=7. The checker programs and exact outputs are included. Finite computation is used only for finite exhaustive statements.

value.rationale: At the intrinsic chromatic palette size of a canonical vertex-transitive, strongly regular graph, the full recoloring state space has two equal nontrivial components even though there are no frozen optimal colorings. The global permutation parity identifies a structural obstruction. The precise palette increase to six restores connectivity, and a separate Grundy argument extends it to every larger palette, answering a natural graph-specific mixing-threshold question. The exact degree strata distinguish configurations and support future structural/reconfiguration analysis; a finite result is adequate because the defined graph and invariant are natural, not an ad hoc sliced table.
